reviewMethod: Compared the captured English blocks and six chronological samples across the full recorded duration of each of 32 existing source clips: male/female, front/side, eight exercises. Editorial corrections resolve visible equipment, support or return-motion conflicts; these are not recovered provider wording. No load, set, repetition or angle prescriptions are invented.

decisions.changeReason: Both genders visibly support the hold on their forearms and toes, with elbows forward of the shoulders. No hand-plank-to-elbow walking transition is shown. Replace the contradictory starting support while retaining the long lever and hold cues.
steps: Start in a forearm plank with your elbows farther forward than your shoulders, until your ears are between your biceps. Support your body on your forearms and toes.
Hold in this position for the allotted amount of time.
Make sure you keep a flat back for the whole set.

decisions.changeReason: Both genders sit on a bench with a kettlebell on each thigh near the knee, hands steadying the handles. There is no barbell. Heels rise and return while the forefeet remain supported on the floor.
steps: Start by sitting on a bench with one kettlebell resting on each thigh near your knees. Your feet should be flat on the ground, about hip-width apart.
Hold the kettlebells steady with your hands and lift your heels off the ground.
Hold this position for a moment, then slowly lower your heels back to the ground.

decisions.changeReason: Both genders hold one kettlebell in each hand, not two per hand, while the front foot stays on a low plate and the rear leg bends behind them. Correct only the load quantity in the first step.
steps: Place your foot on a plate or a low box. Hold one kettlebell in each hand.
Put all of your weight on your front foot and lean forward.
Lower until your calves touch your hamstrings and then extend back up.

decisions.changeReason: The clips show alternating knee drives from hand support, with each leg extending back before the opposite knee advances. Remove the conflicting 'quickly switch' cue and unnecessary foot-near-hand instruction; retain the explicit slow-tempo intent already present in the source's final step without adding a numeric cadence.
steps: To perform a bodyweight mountain climber, start in a plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders.
Slowly bring your right knee towards your chest, then extend that leg back and bring your left knee towards your chest.
Continue this movement, alternating legs, at a slow pace for a set amount of time or repetitions.

decisions.changeReason: Both genders keep one dumbbell at each shoulder through the step-up and descent; no barbell is present. Remove the overhand-only grip prescription and retain the source's explicit right-up/left-down sequence as an example, not a claim that both clips use the same leading side.
steps: Stand in front of a step or bench with your feet shoulder-width apart and hold one dumbbell at each shoulder.
Step up onto the bench with your right foot, pushing off your foot to raise your body up onto the bench.
Bring your left foot up onto the bench and stand up straight, keeping the dumbbells at your shoulders.
Step back down with your left foot, followed by your right foot, to return to the starting position.

decisions.changeReason: Both genders have their feet suspended in the TRX foot cradles while their shoulders and arms stay on the floor; the feet are not flat on the floor. Hip raising and lowering are visible, so make the suspended support and return explicit in the existing three-step block.
steps: Lie on your back with your feet supported in the foot cradles of the TRX straps and your knees bent. Keep your feet suspended off the ground.
Place your arms by your sides with your palms facing down.
Drive your hips up towards the ceiling, squeezing your glutes and hamstrings at the top of the movement, then lower your hips back down under control.

decisions.changeReason: Both genders keep their feet on a stability ball, not on a bar, while raising and lowering the hips. Correct the support object in the second step only.
steps: Start by lying flat on your back with your feet resting on top of a ball.
Push through your heels and raise your hips towards the ceiling, keeping your feet on the ball.
Engage your glutes at the top of the movement, pause briefly and then lower your hips back down to the starting position.

decisions.changeReason: Both genders press two low-anchored bands overhead and then bend the elbows to return their hands toward shoulder level. The source's straight-arm return conflicts with that motion. Correct only the return cue; keep the setup and press.
steps: Stand between the two anchored bands, grasp them with an overhand grip, and position the bands at shoulder level.
Brace your core and push the bands overhead, fully extending your arms.
Lower the bands back to shoulder level by bending your elbows, keeping your core engaged. Repeat for desired number of reps.
